newsitem.title: NORWAY: Former Norway premier to quit parliament too.
newsitem.headline: Former Norway premier to quit parliament too.

text.p: Gro Harlem Brundtland, who resigned as Norway's prime minister two months ago, announced on Saturday that she would quit parliament next year.

Brundtland, who dominated Norwegian politics for more than a decade, surprisingly stepped down as premier on October 25, but had been expected to remain a member of parliament for the ruling Labour Party.
"Yesterday I contacted the Oslo Labour Party to say that I will not run for parliament in the autumn of 1997," Brundtland said in a statement distributed by the national news agency NTB.
She was referring to the general election next September.

Brundtland, 57, who is writing a book about her three terms as premier and who has often been mentioned in the past as a possible candidate for the job of U.N. secretary-general, cited family reasons for her decision.

Brundtland's announcement coincided with a report in the tabloid Verdens Gang which said she was unhappy with the way her successor, Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland, had dealt with a recent political scandal involving the intelligence service.

Parliament was up in arms recently after finding out that the intelligence service has secretly looked into the background of Berge Furre, a prominent left-wing politician assigned to examine the spy organisation's own activities.
Jagland unceremoniously dumped Energy Minister Grete Faremo, a government minister since 1990, on December 16 because of the scandal which stemmed from her time as justice minister last year.
Verdens Gang quoted Labour Party parliamentary sources as saying Brundtland thought Jagland, buckling under pressure from a hostile parliament, had been too quick in forcing Faremo out of office.
Faremo, 41, was one of the most trusted ministers in the former government of Brundtland, a tough political veteran who was known to back her ministers to the hilt.

Separately, Faremo announced on Saturday that she was also giving up her nomination for parliament in the next election. She said she was fed up with politics after being kicked out of office for a scandal she was never directly involved in.
"I must admit that what has happened has deprived me of energy and the wish to work with politics on the top level," Faremo told NTB.
